prompts.display_text: Pin a European country with a dedicated temple.
prompts.text_original: Pin a European country with at least one dedicated temple (as of October 2026).
prompts.summary: Europe's first temple was dedicated near Bern, Switzerland, in 1955, followed by London in 1958. As of October 2026, twelve European countries had a dedicated temple, the most recent being Rome, Italy, and Lisbon, Portugal, both in 2019.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country or territory with a temple standing today that Gerrit W. Gong dedicated or rededicated.
prompts.text_original: A country where Gerrit W. Gong dedicated or rededicated a temple now in use (as of October 2026).
prompts.citation: ChurchofJesusChristTemples.org chronological list (dedicated-by column), read 26 Oct 2026
prompts.summary: Gerrit W. Gong has dedicated temples from North America to Africa and Asia. They include Winnipeg Manitoba (2021), the rededication of Hong Kong China (2022), Taylorsville Utah and Puebla Mexico (2024), and Harare Zimbabwe and Miraflores Guatemala City (2026).

prompts.display_text: Pin a Spanish-speaking country that Saints names as reached after Argentina, in the 1940s and 1950s.
prompts.text_original: Saints vol. 4 ch. 4: after Argentina, the gospel spread to these Spanish-speaking countries in the 1940s and 1950s. Pin one.
prompts.summary: Saints volume 4 tells how the Church, after missionaries arrived in Argentina in the 1920s, spread to its Spanish-speaking neighbors. Missionaries entered Uruguay, Guatemala, Costa Rica and El Salvador in the 1940s, and preaching began in Chile, Peru, Honduras, Panama and Paraguay in the 1950s. In 1959 Elder Spencer W. Kimball toured South America to assess the needs of the growing Church there.

prompts.display_text: Pin a present-day country with a city named in Genesis whose site is agreed.
prompts.text_original: A present-day country with a city named in Genesis whose site is agreed
prompts.note: Places in the West Bank or Gaza, such as Bethlehem, Hebron, Jericho or Gaza city, count as Palestine, which is not an answer.
prompts.summary: Genesis moves across the ancient Near East. Abraham's family set out from Ur, stopped at Haran, and Abraham and Isaac lived around Beersheba. Damascus appears in Abraham's story (Genesis 14:15), Joseph married the daughter of the priest of On in Egypt, and Jacob named Mahanaim and Penuel east of the Jordan (Genesis 32).

answers.name: Iraq
answers.fact: Ur, Babel and Nineveh are all in Iraq.

answers.name: Egypt
answers.fact: Joseph married the daughter of the priest of On, Heliopolis (Genesis 41:45).

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: Beersheba is central to Abraham and Isaac's stories.

answers.name: Syria
answers.fact: Damascus is named in Genesis 14:15 and 15:2.

answers.name: Jordan
answers.fact: Jacob named Mahanaim and Penuel, east of the Jordan (Genesis 32).

prompts.display_text: Pin a country that Saints names as covered by the South American missions by 1963.
prompts.text_original: Saints vol. 4 ch. 7: by 1963 the Church's South American missions covered these countries. Pin one.
prompts.summary: By 1963 the Church's missions in South America covered six countries. Brazil and Argentina had two missions each, Uruguay and Chile had one each, and Peru and Bolivia shared one. The first South American mission had opened in Buenos Aires, Argentina, in 1925.

answers.name: Argentina
answers.fact: Had two missions; the first South American mission opened in Buenos Aires in 1925.
